summary: Mark Tatz was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his PhD from the University of British Columbia under Leon Hurvitz, also studying with traditional teachers, and was a professor at the California Institute of Integral Studies.

Mark Teeuwen specializes in Japanology and religious studies. He earned his MA and PhD from Leiden University, lectured at Cardiff University from 1994 to 1999, and became a professor at the University of Oslo in 1999.

Mark Unno works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. Educated at Oberlin College and Stanford University, he held posts at Brown University (~1994–2000) and the University of Oregon (~2000–2007).

Markus Gabriel is a philosopher who studied at the University of Bonn. He has held positions at Bonn, UC Berkeley, The New School, and became a Global Senior Advisor at the Kyoto Institute of Philosophy in 2024.

Markus Viehbeck specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Vienna under Helmut Tauscher and Franz-Karl Ehrhard, worked as a researcher at Heidelberg University, and serves on the faculty at Vienna.

Marsha Weidner is a scholar of Sinology, art history, and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD from UC Berkeley. She held an assistant professorship at the University of Virginia and later became Professor of the History of Art at Kansas.
Marshall Sahlins worked in history and archaeology. Educated at the University of Michigan and Columbia University, he taught at Michigan (~1957–1973) and the University of Chicago from 1973.

Marta Sernesi is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Turin in 2007 and was attested as a visiting professor at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 2026.

Martha Ann Selby is an Indologist who is Professor Emeritus at the University of Texas at Austin. Attested in 2026, she serves as Sangam Professor of South Asian Studies and chair of the Department of South Asian Studies at Harvard University.

Martha Nussbaum is a philosopher educated at NYU and Harvard. She taught at Harvard, Oxford, and Brown before joining the University of Chicago in 1995 as the Ernst Freund Distinguished Service Professor of Law and Ethics.

Martin Baumann is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from Leibniz University Hannover and completed his Habilitation at Leipzig, becoming Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Lucerne in 2001.

Martin Brauen is a Tibetologist who studied at Delhi and Zurich. He held curator and director roles at the Ethnographic Museum of the University of Zurich from 1975 and served as chief curator at the Rubin Museum of Art (2008–2012).

Martin Collcutt specializes in Japanology, history, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Cambridge and Harvard, he taught at Tokyo and Yokohama National universities before serving as Director of the East Asian Studies Program at Princeton University from 1975 to 2015.

Martin Delhey specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, holding posts at Hamburg, Göttingen, Ryukoku University, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Martin Haug was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tübingen, Göttingen, and Bonn. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College (~1859–1866) and later as Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at the University of Munich from 1868.

Martin Heidegger was a philosopher who studied under Heinrich Rickert at the University of Freiburg. He taught at the University of Marburg (1923–1928) and held posts at Freiburg between 1915 and 1940.

Martin Joachim Kümmel is an Indologist and linguist who completed his degrees and Habilitation at the University of Freiburg. He served as an assistant at Freiburg (~1999–2008) and was appointed chairholder at the University of Jena in 2013.

Martin King Whyte is a Sinologist and sociologist educated at Cornell and Harvard. He taught at Boston University, the University of Michigan (1970–1994), George Washington University (1994–2000), and joined Harvard University in 2000.

Martin Lehnert is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Freiburg and was attested as Professor of East Asian Religion and Philosophy at the University of Munich in 2016.

Martin Lowenthal is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under traditional teachers Namkhai Norbu and Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche. He has held academic posts at Boston College and Harvard University.
